title: The Log in the Well
hook: Deac's clipboard is in the well. Write the hours down.
scene: You unfold a metal clipboard that is not yours. Deac left it in the well at the lot with a note in dispatch cadence: date, location, day or night, weather, skills, hours, initials. The Grid does not count as practice unless you write it down. Clear cold midday in a Kent lot, stalls faded, the Menace ticking. You have already used a school zone, a stop, a left, a bike, a bus, a hand, a light, a voice. The clipboard is how the hours become legal. It is also how you notice you have not done space yet.
debrief: Supervised hours are a log, not a feeling. Date, location, day or night, weather, skill, time, initials. If it is not on the sheet, the Grid did not happen.

source.teaching_target: The PSDP log is diegetic: hours only count when written. Space cushion is the next unpaid skill.

image_brief.subject: Ali standing outside in the lot, looking down, filling out a metal clipboard — paper facing her, only the blank brushed-steel back toward the camera
image_brief.foreground: worn black steering wheel and cracked faded pink dash; aftermarket tablet LIT as a digital radio with station name and FM channel readout; welded steel mesh across the glass
image_brief.midground: Ali through the mesh, chest-up, black oversize tee and charcoal work jacket, cranberry hair in a loose shoulder-length curl-out with no crown braids, pen in her right hand writing, clipboard tilted toward her so the log is hidden
image_brief.background: a Kent parking lot, one low gray commercial building behind her, faded empty stalls, clear cold midday, no sun flare, no readable signage
image_brief.read: she is outside writing the hours; you only see the metal back of the board; the tablet radio is on
